name: Molina Healthcare, Inc.
moat_justification: Weak-to-moderate moat: pure-play government-programs expertise (~8% national Medicaid share, multi-year state contracts, low 6.5% G&A ratio, experience with complex dual-eligible and long-term-care populations) gives incumbency and RFP credibility, but the customer is the state — pricing is set by rate-setting that lagged medical trend badly in 2025-26, contracts are periodically rebid and can be lost, providers are contracted not owned, and scale is well below UnitedHealthcare/Elevance/Centene. Return evidence is thin and deteriorating: gross margin (1 minus MCR) was 15.9% in FY2023, 15.3% in FY2024 and 13.1% in FY2025 (fundamentals.json), operating margin fell 4.6% to 1.7% over the same years, and the roic_proxy series is not meaningful here — it divides by equity + debt minus cash only, so regulated subsidiary cash/investments held against claims and government liabilities drive it to absurd levels (e.g. 10.94 in FY2020); the margin series is the usable evidence and it does not support a moat above 4.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 3.3%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share -12.91 vs 3-yr median 7.42 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
one_liner: Weak-moat (4/10) government managed-care payer in a rate/trend trough — normalized owner's earnings are $7.42/share but at $207.05 the weighted IRR is only 6.1% (IV@15% $59.44); it clears the 15% hurdle only at or below ~$59.
moat_for: Pure-play government-programs focus — ~8% national Medicaid share and expertise in complex, high-acuity populations states struggle to manage
Multi-year state Medicaid contracts with incumbency/RFP track record — retained Illinois, renewed Wisconsin, won the Florida Children's Medical Services contract (~$6B annual premium at full scale)
Low cost structure — G&A ratio 6.5% in FY2025, below diversified payer peers, from the focused footprint
Integrated dual-eligible (Medicaid + Medicare) offering aligned with where state and federal policy is pushing enrollment
moat_against: No pricing power — premium rates are set by states/CMS and lagged medical cost trend in 2025-26 (Medicaid MCR guided 92.9% for 2026); margin recovery depends on future rate cycles, not Molina's own pricing
Contracts are rebid and losable — membership fell 14% YoY to ~4.9M by Q2 2026 on Medicaid market contraction, contract expirations and Marketplace exits
Subscale vs UnitedHealthcare, Elevance and Centene in purchasing, provider rates and diversification
Providers are contracted, not owned — no owned care delivery to control medical trend directly
Single-customer-type concentration — effectively all revenue is government premium, exposed to Medicaid redeterminations, ACA subsidy expiry and state budgets
